text:
Morgan: FYI noticing autoscaler not scaling our GPU nodegroup in prod after the 1.28 control plane upgrade.
Ravi: which pool? gpupool-east? logs?
Morgan: gpupool-gpu-east-2 (the one tagged node.k8s.redwood/gpu=true). No new nodes come up even though pending pods queued for >5m.
Sasha: can you paste the CA logs (deploy: cluster-autoscaler) from around the scale event?
Morgan: sure, here's the relevant tail:
```
I0318 12:04:22.123456       1 scale_up.go:345] NoScale: no node group found with matching provider id
E0318 12:04:22.123467       1 autoprovision.go:87] provider api mismatch: unknown field "nodeGroupRef" in v1alpha1.NodeGroup
```
Chris: hm that error smells like the NodeGroup CRD contract changed in the new k8s provider library. We saw providerlib bumped in the 1.28 upgrade PR earlier.
Ravi: did the nodepool operator upgrade too? If the control plane moved first but the nodegroup controller stayed at old CRD schema CA might be reading different objects.
Morgan: nodepool-operator is still at 0.9.2 (deployed yesterday), cluster was upgraded to 1.28.0-rc. kubelet on existing nodes is unchanged until drain. New node bootstrap fails to register with expected providerID shape.
Sasha: quick verification commands:
```
kubectl get nodegroups -A -o yaml | head -n 80
kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/cluster-autoscaler | grep nodeGroup
```
Morgan: output shows NodeGroup apiVersion: infra.redwood.io/v1alpha1 but CA is expecting v1beta1 with 'providerNodeID' instead of 'providerID'.
autoscaler-bot: incident-created id=INC-2026-0318-01 summary="CA unable to match NodeGroup schema after upgrade" severity=high
Chris: immediate mitigations:
- revert control plane to previous patch (if available) on one affected cluster as a canary
- patch CA to tolerate both fields (fast) and roll in canary
- update nodepool-operator and NodeGroup CRD to v1beta1 and do a rolling restart of controllers
Ravi: patching CA to be permissive sounds fastest. We can add code to fallback from providerID -> providerNodeID. Could also add a temporary webhook that injects providerNodeID from providerID on NodeGroup create/patch.
Sasha: I can spin up a quick hotfix build: change lookup in scale_up.go to try both fields, add unit test. How long to get image through our CI? ~45m to 1h.
Morgan: timeline ok. Meanwhile we should avoid draining GPU nodes in other clusters until we confirm fix.
Ravi: adding a K8s patch is easier ops-side. Example patch we can apply as a one-off mutating webhook replacement (quick and dirty):
```
kubectl patch nodegroup gpupool-gpu-east-2 -n infra --type='json' -p='[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/providerNodeID","value":"$(kubectl get nodegroup gpupool-gpu-east-2 -n infra -o jsonpath='{.spec.providerID}')"}]'
```
But that's hacky and only for that object.
Chris: go for both: Sasha to open CA hotfix PR and I will put up an ops playbook to patch NodeGroup resources if short-term needed. Also create a dashboard for number of NodeGroup schema mismatches.
Morgan: CA hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood/autoscaler/pull/463
Sasha: PR created, CI green on unit tests. Requesting review @Chris @Ravi. I added fallback in FindMatchingNodeGroup() and a log explaining fallback.
Chris: reviewed, lgtm. Can we run image in staging first? We have a staging cluster already on 1.28.
Sasha: deploying to staging now: `kubectl -n kube-system set image deploy/cluster-autoscaler cluster-autoscaler=ghcr.io/redwood/autoscaler:hotfix-463-20260318`
Morgan: staging scaled up gpupool-gpu-east-2 successfully. Verified pods bound to newly created GPU nodes.
Ravi: great. Next steps:
- Roll hotfix to prod in a canary (one AZ) 30min observation window
- Backport CRD changes: nodepool-operator upgrade to 0.10.0 which includes v1beta1 NodeGroup, schedule for tomorrow
- Add an e2e test that simulates provider API shape drift during upgrade
- Postmortem note in incidents channel with root cause: control plane/library bump + operator/crd version skew
Morgan: I'll create the incident doc and include the patch and PR links. Also adding cost note: while this was out we had ~12 pending GPU pods for 40m -> ~240 GPU-minutes queued, cost impact ~ $120 (estimate). Put that in the incident writeup.
autoscaler-bot: runbook-updated id=RB-CA-01 status=staged
Chris: thanks everyone. Lessons: don't upgrade control plane without the operator/crd compatibility gate and add schema-forward compatibility in CA to accept older/newer fields.
Sasha: I'll open follow-up issues: one for operator backport, one for CA graceful schema handling, and one e2e test. Assigning to infra-ops squad.
Morgan: closing loop: applying canary to prod in 10m. Will post results.
Sasha: canary succeeded, scaling worked in AZ-a. Rolling full prod deploy now.
Morgan: prod deploy finished. All clusters reporting normal autoscaling. Will file postmortem shortly.
